notes: This catalogue is extracted from the accompanying Markdown reference.
A runtime_candidate is not a guarantee that the command exists in the installed OpenOCD build.
Before execution, check command availability and execution stage with the running OpenOCD instance.
Configuration-only commands must be applied before OpenOCD initialization, normally through startup configuration.
Driver identifiers are not standalone commands; they are values used by driver registration/configuration commands.
Procedures and helper functions may only be available when the relevant OpenOCD scripts have been sourced.
The AI may select commands, but the MCP implementation must validate arguments, state and safety before execution.

mode_guide.[Command]: General command; candidate for runtime Tcl RPC after availability and state checks.
mode_guide.[Overridable Procedure]: Tcl procedure that may be overridden or supplied by scripts.
mode_guide.[Function]: Jim-Tcl helper function; check whether it is defined in the active interpreter.
mode_guide.Driver identifiers: Identifiers used by adapter, flash, NAND, FPGA or trace-port configuration.

entries.name: command mode
entries.description: Returns the execution stage allowed for a given command: `'any'`, `'config'`, or `'exec'`. If `command_name` is omitted, returns the current server execution mode. If an unknown command is supplied, returns `'unknown'`. - **Example**: command mode adapter driver

entries.name: init
entries.description: Explicitly terminates the configuration stage and transitions OpenOCD into the run stage. This command validates the configured JTAG scan chain, probes hardware, initializes targets, DAPs, flash controllers, and starts server listeners. If omitted in configuration scripts, OpenOCD calls `init` implicitly at the conclusion of script parsing. - **Internal Chain**: `init` automatically executes the following subsystem initializers: 1. `target init` `[Config Command]` 2. `transport init` `[Command]` 3. `dap init` `[Command]` 4. `flash init` `[Config Command]` 5. `nand init` `[Config Command]` 6. `pld init` `[Config Command]` 7. `tpiu init` `[Command]` 8. Evaluates all callbacks in the `post_init_commands` Tcl list. - **Example**:

entries.name: noinit
entries.description: Disables the automatic implicit execution of `init` at the conclusion of startup script processing. Allows developers to connect over Telnet or Tcl while OpenOCD remains in the configuration stage to issue interactive configuration commands. The user must manually call `init` to start debugging.

entries.name: jtag_init
entries.description: Invoked during server startup to verify communication with the configured JTAG scan chain. The default implementation first runs `jtag arp_init` (lightweight reset). If validation fails, it invokes `init_reset` for a full reset before re-examining the chain.

entries.name: gdb_port
entries.description: Queries or configures the TCP port for GDB connections. - Omitted argument: Displays currently configured GDB port.

entries.name: telnet_port
entries.description: Queries or specifies the TCP port on which OpenOCD listens for incoming interactive Telnet connections (intended for human operators). Default port is `4444`. Set to `"disabled"` to deactivate.

entries.name: tcl_port
entries.description: Queries or configures the TCP port for headless Tcl RPC client connections (intended for machine interfaces, automated test frameworks, and IDE plugins). Default port is `6666`. Set to `"disabled"` to deactivate.

entries.name: bindto
entries.description: Specifies the IPv4 network interface or hostname to which TCP servers (GDB, Telnet, Tcl) bind. By default, OpenOCD binds strictly to `127.0.0.1` (loopback) for security. Use `bindto 0.0.0.0` to permit remote network connections across a local network.

entries.name: shutdown
entries.description: Gracefully shuts down the OpenOCD daemon, disconnecting all active GDB, Telnet, and RPC sessions. If `error` is specified, OpenOCD exits with a non-zero exit code. Triggers all callbacks registered in the `pre_shutdown_commands` Tcl list. - **Example**: lappend pre_shutdown_commands { echo "Session complete. Turning off power." } shutdown

entries.name: exit
entries.description: Closes the current interactive Telnet session without shutting down the OpenOCD server process.

entries.name: help / usage
entries.description: Displays command help strings or parameter usage text. If `string` is supplied, filters output to matching commands.

entries.name: sleep
entries.description: Suspends script execution for at least `msec` milliseconds. If `busy` is specified, executes a tight spinloop instead of releasing the CPU (strongly discouraged).

entries.name: debug_level
entries.description: Displays or sets the verbosity level of server logging (0 to 4):

entries.name: echo
entries.description: Prints `message` to the server log and active Telnet session at user priority. `-n` suppresses the trailing newline.

entries.name: log_output
entries.description: Redirects logging messages to a file, or restores default output (`stderr`).

entries.name: add_script_search_dir
entries.description: Appends `directory` to OpenOCD's search path for configuration scripts and auxiliary data files.

entries.name: find / ocd_find
entries.description: Resolves and returns the full absolute path to `<filename>` by evaluating OpenOCD's search directories in priority order.

entries.name: adapter speed
entries.description: Sets the maximum clock frequency of the adapter interface in kHz (e.g., `3000` for 3 MHz). Value `0` enables adaptive clocking (RTCK) if supported by the adapter and target. - **Example**: `adapter speed 4000`

entries.description: Provides unified, generic GPIO mapping for bitbanging and SoC GPIO adapters. Configures signal direction, active polarity, output drive stage, pull resistors, and initial states.

entries.name: flash bank
entries.syntax: flash bank name driver base size chip_width bus_width target [driver_options]
entries.description: Registers a persistent flash bank covering memory from `base` to `base + size - 1`. Links the bank to driver `driver` and execution target `target`. - **Example**: flash bank $_FLASHNAME stm32f4x 0x08000000 0 0 0 $_TARGETNAME

entries.name: flash banks
entries.description: Prints a formatted summary of all declared flash banks, base addresses, sizes, and driver types.

entries.name: flash list
entries.description: Returns a structured Tcl list of associative arrays describing declared flash devices.

entries.name: flash probe
entries.description: Interrogates flash controller hardware to identify chip geometry, sector boundaries, and capacity.

entries.name: flash erase_sector
entries.description: Erases sectors in bank `num` from index `first` to `last` (inclusive). Using `last` as the end index erases to bank conclusion.

entries.name: flash erase_address
entries.description: Erases flash sectors spanning `address` to `address + length - 1`. `pad` extends boundaries to cover whole sectors. `unlock` removes sector protection before erasing.

entries.name: flash write_bank
entries.description: Programs raw binary file `filename` to flash bank `num` starting at `offset`.

entries.name: flash read_bank
entries.description: Dumps `length` bytes from bank `num` at `offset` into binary file `filename`.

entries.name: flash verify_bank
entries.description: Verifies bank contents against binary file `filename`.

entries.name: flash write_image
entries.description: Automatically programs loadable sections of an image file (`elf`, `hex`, `s19`, `bin`) into mapped flash banks. `erase` erases affected sectors beforehand; `unlock` unprotects flash.

entries.name: flash verify_image
entries.description: Verifies mapped flash banks against image `filename`.

entries.name: flash erase_check
entries.description: Verifies whether sectors in bank `num` are in erased state (`0xFF`).

entries.name: flash info
entries.description: Displays hardware protection status, lock blocks, and sector geometry for bank `num`.

entries.name: flash protect
entries.description: Enables (`on`) or disables (`off`) write protection for blocks in bank `num`.

entries.name: flash padded_value
entries.description: Sets fill byte value for padding sector alignments (default `0xff`).

entries.name: flash filld / fillw / fillh / fillb
entries.description: Fills flash blocks with repeated 64-bit, 32-bit, 16-bit, or 8-bit pattern without prior erase.

entries.name: flash mdd / mdw / mdh / mdb
entries.description: Reads flash memory through driver access methods, allowing inspection of banks not mapped directly into CPU address space.

entries.name: program
entries.description: High-level monolithic Jim-Tcl helper procedure that executes `init`, `reset init`, `flash write_image erase`, optional pre-verify/verify, reset, and shutdown.

entries.name: drscan
entries.description: Shifts fields into the Data Register of `tap` while all other TAPs are held in `BYPASS`. Returns the previous register contents shifted out of TDO. `tap_state` sets end state (defaults to `run/idle`).

entries.name: irscan
entries.description: Loads instruction opcodes into the Instruction Registers of specified TAPs while placing remaining TAPs in `BYPASS`.

entries.name: pathmove
entries.description: Transitions the JTAG TAP finite state machine through an explicit series of legal state transitions, one TCK cycle per state. States must be stable or legal next-states.

entries.name: runtest
entries.description: Transitions FSM to `Run-Test/Idle` and pulses TCK for at least `num_cycles`.

entries.name: flush_count
entries.description: Returns the count of JTAG queue flushes across the host USB/Ethernet link (useful for batching performance optimization).

entries.name: verify_ircapture
entries.description: Validates that ircapture returns the standard `...01` binary pattern during IR scans.

entries.name: verify_jtag
entries.description: Validates both DR and IR scan integrity.

entries.name: svf
entries.description: Resets TAP state machine and executes Serial Vector Format test vectors from `filename`.

entries.name: xsvf
entries.description: Executes binary Xilinx Serial Vector Format files for FPGA/CPLD configuration. `virt2` interprets delay counts as TCK cycles instead of microseconds.

entries.name: ipdbg
entries.description: Starts or stops an IPDBG JTAG-Host TCP gateway server for internal logic analyzer and waveform generator IP cores.

entries.name: memTestDataBus
entries.description: Performs a walking 1's test on the target data bus at `address` to detect open pins, shorts to VDD/GND, and solder bridges.

entries.name: memTestAddressBus
entries.description: Performs walking 1's test across address bits to detect address line aliasing and stuck-at faults.

entries.name: memTestDevice
entries.description: Verifies storage cell integrity by performing increment/decrement patterns across the entire memory range, verifying every bit as `0` and `1`.

entries.name: runAllMemTests
entries.description: Executes `memTestDataBus`, `memTestAddressBus`, and `memTestDevice` sequentially across the specified RAM block.

entries.name: gdb_breakpoint_override
entries.description: Forces breakpoint allocation type for incoming GDB break commands. Overcomes limitations of IDEs that fail to differentiate hardware vs. software breakpoints.

entries.name: gdb_flash_program
entries.description: Enables OpenOCD to execute flash programming upon receiving GDB `vFlash` packets during `load` commands (default: `enable`).

entries.name: gdb_memory_map
entries.description: Transmits target memory map XML descriptions to GDB via `qXfer:memory-map:read` packets (default: `enable`).

entries.name: gdb_report_data_abort
entries.description: Specifies whether memory access data aborts return error packets to GDB (default: `disable`).

entries.name: gdb_report_register_access_error
entries.description: Returns error packets when GDB attempts reading/writing unsupported registers (default: `disable`).

entries.name: gdb_target_description
entries.description: Transmits architectural register descriptions to GDB via `qXfer:features:read` packets (default: `enable`).

entries.name: gdb_save_tdesc
entries.description: Dumps target XML register description file (`target_name.xml`) to the local file system.

entries.name: capture
entries.description: Executes arbitrary OpenOCD command string `<command>` and intercepts all server log output generated during execution, returning the log text as a single Tcl result string. - **Example**: set log_data [capture "reset init"] echo "Captured log: $log_data"
